chapter: Lester Nelson and New Orleans players
title: Playing requests, favourite songs and his organ
summary: Treats every request as his favourite, his wife's sense of timing, what he plays at home, and moving his organ for jobs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I've got to go in there in a minute and bring out a stack of them. Uh-huh. And they're all, all the way from the Ave Maria's to golden slippers and all.
Yeah. But you know how to play all this many things. Yeah. You can't feel the same about all of it, I know. You must have...
You're ready to hear the answer.

Yeah, we're ready. Yeah. Yeah. I just wanted to say that we've got Pam Tala interviewing Jeff Riddick now, the third reel, so he can answer her question instead of me. You're close enough to the mic, Pam. Okay.

There are 10,000 people, for instance, in a gathering, and I'm playing. And maybe out of that 10,000 people, I may get 20 written requests, or I may not get one. I never know. But I always had the attitude this, that if that was your favorite tune while I was playing it, then it was my favorite tune. And that's the only way that I can give you an answer to it, because I always had that idea. And I never will forget one time, Hip Ginley once said, the prettiest thing about a tune is the tune.
Well, what about you and your wife? Did you all have a favorite song? Favorite songs?
No, my wife can't carry a tune in a sack. She's tone pitch deaf, if you want to term it that way. She's not gifted for music, the sound, but the timing, she is absolutely marvelous with it.
Okay, we can swap now. What do you play for yourself, Jeff?
You just sit down and play.

I might sit down and play. I just, the mood might come to me when I sit down, and it may leave me the minute I play ten measures. I don't know. Now, I play organ, and I have an organ out there, which I'll be very happy to. It's in a cottage out there in my backyard. It's ready to play at all times. I have to keep it ready because it's electronic. And I move it on quite a few convention jobs and things like that. But I have to charge so much, I will not leave home with that organ for less than $200. It costs me $50 to move it. And the work that's taxed to it.
